title: Were Nazis Drug-Fueled Crankheads?
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the drug use of the Nazi regime, drawing mainly on Norman Ohler's book Blitzed. They cover Weimar-era drug culture and Germany's role as a major cocaine and morphine producer, the Nazi crackdown on addicts and the 'degenerate' label, the rollout of the methamphetamine-based drug Pervitin to the German military (including the Wehrmacht's blitzkrieg pushes into Poland and France and the later Russian campaign collapse), the experimental drug D IX, and Hitler's personal physician Theodore Morell, who injected him with a cocktail of drugs for about nine years. The episode closes with a listener mail story about a high school pantsing during an attempted asking-out.

segments.title: Introduction and Norman Ohler's Blitzed
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on Nazi drug use and recommend Norman Ohler's book Blitzed, which argues drugs shaped the Third Reich. They note that drugs were not the sole cause of the Holocaust, pointing to early 1933 Dachau killings.

segments.title: Weimar Republic drug culture and Nazi crackdown
segments.summary: The Weimar Republic's jazz-age drug culture is described, with Germany producing much of the world's morphine and cocaine in the 1920s. The Nazis attacked drug users and 'degenerate art' and promoted family, home and church.

segments.title: Pervitin and synthetic stimulants in Germany
segments.summary: German firms moved to synthetic stimulants, including Pervitin, a methamphetamine-type drug first sold over the counter. The Temmler firm and chemist Fritz Hauschild are mentioned, and the military then adopted the drug under a stimulant decree pushed by Otto Ranke.

segments.title: Speed in the German military and blitzkrieg
segments.summary: Pervitin was distributed to soldiers and pilots, sometimes as chocolate, with more than 35 million doses made between April and July 1940. Soldiers reportedly believed it fueled rapid advances in Poland and France, including a nonstop three-day push into France.

segments.title: Long-term effects and the Russian campaign
segments.summary: Hosts discuss how long-term Pervitin use caused sleep deprivation, psychosis, poor decisions and crashes, and how this weakened German forces during the Russian winter campaign. They also mention experimental drug D IX tested on concentration camp inmates.

segments.title: Theodore Morell and Hitler's injections
segments.summary: Dermatologist Theodore Morell became Hitler's private physician in 1936 and treated his digestive problems and flatulence. Over about nine years he gave Hitler injections of up to dozens of drugs, including cocaine, morphine, OxyContin precursors and Vitamultin, and cocaine eye drops and snorting.

segments.title: Morell's motives, Hitler's decline and aftermath
segments.summary: Morell's commercial drug business and his letter to the Reich Health Office are discussed, along with Hitler's decline, Parkinson's-like symptoms, and Strychnine-containing gas pills. Ohler's view that the drugs clouded Hitler's judgment is covered, and Morell's fate: fired in April 1945 and interrogated by the Allies.

segments.title: Mutaflor and Hitler's probiotic
segments.summary: The hosts describe Mutaflor, a probiotic bacteria strain isolated in 1917 from a World War One soldier's stool, which Hitler reportedly took and which is illegal in the US.

segments.title: Listener mail: pantsing story
segments.summary: A listener recounts being pantsed by a friend in high school just as he asked a girl out in front of the class. The hosts react and mention an earlier rumor about a classmate.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts recommend Blitzed and invite listeners to send their own cringe stories, then sign off.
